verdict.statement: Every taxonomy, derivation, trust-order and provenance property of v1.10 verifies, and the restored reducer is exhaustively equivalent to the authenticated predecessor across 696,384 independently constructed comparisons. The candidate is nonetheless REJECTED because it does not achieve its own stated purpose: it asserts that v1.9's bytes were insufficient for an RT15 pin-only rebind and positions itself as the sufficient replacement, but a pin-only rebind of RT14 onto v1.10 fails. The compatibility surface was derived from the one export v1.9 dropped rather than from RT14's actual d9mod usage.

blockingFindings.title: v1.10 restores reduce_concurrent but not V17, so an RT15 pin-only rebind of RT14 still fails
blockingFindings.evidence: RT14 (check-retention-custody-v14.py) accesses four attributes on the D9 module: V17, derive_class, derive_codes and reduce_concurrent. Line 472 evaluates d9mod.V17.V16.derive_class(first_axes). v1.8, RT14's current pin, exposes V17 (a module handle onto check-d9-v1.7.py, which in turn exposes V16). v1.9 exposes neither V17 nor reduce_concurrent. v1.10 restores reduce_concurrent but STILL does not expose V17. The string 'V17' occurs zero times in d9-exit-contract.v1.10.json, and v19CompatibilityDisposition.requiredPublicExports lists only the four named symbols.
blockingFindings.reproducibleCondition: In a disposable copy of the artifacts tree, apply a pin-only rebind to RT14: set D9_CHECKER to check-d9-v1.10.py and its PINS entry to 77f86334…, changing nothing else. Run the RT14 checker. It exits 1 with 'RT14-TOTALITY-EXCEPTION: controlled malformed shape (AttributeError)'. Isolated directly: v1.8 resolves d9mod.V17.V16.derive_class successfully, while v1.10 raises AttributeError: module has no attribute 'V17'.
blockingFindings.whyTheAuthoredSuiteMissedIt: The candidate's RT14-compatibility probe asserts only that the byte string 'd9mod.reduce_concurrent(' appears in the pinned RT14 snapshot. It confirms the reducer is invoked but never enumerates RT14's complete d9mod attribute surface, so a second missing attribute is invisible to it. The contract's requiredPublicExports was likewise populated from the diff against v1.9 rather than from the consumer.
blockingFindings.impact: The immediate downstream instruction is 'D9 v1.10 PASS → author RT15 pin-only successor'. A PASS here would authorise an RT15 that cannot load its own D9 dependency, deferring the failure to the RT15 review or, worse, into the E8 binding gate. The defect class is the same as the v1.8 rejection: an artifact asserting a compatibility property it does not deliver.
blockingFindings.requiredRepair: Derive the required export set FROM the frozen consumer rather than from the predecessor diff. Concretely: enumerate every attribute RT14 accesses on the D9 module, restore all of them — V17 in addition to reduce_concurrent — extend v19CompatibilityDisposition.requiredPublicExports to the complete set, and replace the substring probe with one that resolves every enumerated attribute (including chained access such as V17.V16.derive_class) against the candidate module. Alternatively, if V17 is deliberately withdrawn, state that plainly and record that RT15 cannot be pin-only, since RT14's use-site would then require change.
blockingFindings.confidence: CERTAIN — demonstrated by direct attribute resolution and by an end-to-end simulated rebind

residuals.statement: As in v1.9, the checker authenticates everything it executes but nothing authenticates check-d9-v1.10.py itself. Callers must obtain it by an externally pinned hash and invoke it with -B. Not a defect; a checker cannot bootstrap its own authenticity.

v1.10's selftest constructs and executes attacker-shaped payloads as positive controls, including a marshalled .pyc loaded via SourcelessFileLoader and a mutated predecessor executed in-process, to prove the payloads are genuinely side-effectful before demonstrating the trust boundary defeats them. All such activity is confined to tempfile.TemporaryDirectory and I confirmed it never writes the artifacts tree. This is good adversarial practice, but reviewers should know the checker deliberately runs hostile code in-process.

The v1.9 independent review pinned by this candidate was authored by this reviewer. Its PASS is not independently corroborated here; only the continued integrity of v1.9's two repairs was re-verified with fresh probes.

Carried forward from the v1.9 review: D9 correctly routes custody-provenance proof to RT/E8, and this review again did not verify that RT or E8 discharge it. If neither does, the disclaimer relocated the obligation rather than closing it.
Design-integrity evidence only. No property is QUALIFIED or DEMONSTRATED, no implementation exists, and product release remains unaffected by this review.
